# Learned instinct: pci-no-sad-storage (confidence 1)

Sensitive Authentication Data (SAD — CVV, full track data, PIN blocks) must never be stored after authorization, regardless of encryption. Any task or template that writes SAD to a file, database, log, or variable is a CRITICAL violation that must immediately be escalated to the security team. The agent must block and refuse to author any such code.

Source: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req 3.3.1 — do not retain SAD after authorization
